turns.text: OK. OK. And has this happened to you in your ankle before?

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK, and is there anything that makes the pain better or worse?

turns.text: OK, and anything that makes it better?

turns.label: Patient

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK, have you notice any fevers or chills?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: No.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK, any pain in any other joints besides your ankle?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: No, just my my right ankle.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK, any appetite or weight changes?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: No, I've been I've been just training for this race coming up, so I mean I've been just trying to work on my fitness a little bit, but my weight has been relatively stable.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK, any weakness in your right right extremities or any kind of numbness or tingling sensation?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: No numbness or tingling and no muscle weakness either.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: Ok, right. Have you been diagnosed with any medical conditions in the past?

turns.text: OK. Alright, so I just have a few questions. Right now over your right ankle, do you have, so you mentioned you don't have any swelling, but do you notice any kind of redness or warmth at all?

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK. And are you able to stand up and walk or are you not able to do that right now?

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: Ok, yeah, so definitely what we'll do is we might need to get like a proper physical examination done to make sure there is no fracture. However, if we find that on physical examination you are having significant pain on palpation or any kind of bony pain, we might also require you to get an X Ray of the right foot and ankle, as well as just your lower leg.
